teaching_point: Erythema toxicum neonatorum: blotchy erythematous macules with small central papules/pustules on a well baby — spares palms/soles; self-limiting.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Toxic erythema of the newborn (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/toxic-erythema-of-the-newborn

teaching_point: ETN close-up: fleeting erythematous macules and tiny pustules that wax and wane over days; infant otherwise well — no treatment needed.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Toxic erythema of the newborn (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/toxic-erythema-of-the-newborn

teaching_point: Widespread ETN pattern on trunk — reassure parents; key differentials are infection, TNPM and miliaria.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Toxic erythema of the newborn (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/skin-conditions-in-newborn-babies

teaching_point: Transient neonatal pustular melanosis: fragile pustules on a non-erythematous base, present at birth — more often recognised in darker skin.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Neonatal pustular melanosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/transient-neonatal-pustular-melanosis

teaching_point: TNPM after pustules rupture: hyperpigmented macules with a collarette of scale that fade over weeks to months.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Neonatal pustular melanosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/transient-neonatal-pustular-melanosis

teaching_point: TNPM on trunk/flexures: sterile neutrophilic pustules then residual pigment — benign; culture if infection cannot be excluded.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Transient neonatal pustular melanosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/transient-neonatal-pustular-melanosis

teaching_point: Miliaria (heat rash): crops of clear vesicles or red papules from occluded sweat ducts — cool the baby and remove excess clothing/wraps.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Miliaria (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/miliaria

teaching_point: Miliaria rubra on neck/upper trunk of a neonate — common in overheated babies; settles with cooling (vs ETN or infection).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Miliaria (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/miliaria

teaching_point: Neonatal cephalic pustulosis / neonatal acne: facial papules and pustules in first weeks — usually Malassezia-related; often self-limiting.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Neonatal cephalic pustulosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/neonatal-cephalic-pustulosis

teaching_point: Infantile acne (weeks–months of age): comedones, papules and pustules on cheeks — may scar; distinguish from neonatal cephalic pustulosis.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Infantile acne (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/infantile-acne

teaching_point: Irritant napkin dermatitis: confluent erythema on convex surfaces in contact with wet nappy, typically sparing deep folds.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Napkin dermatitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/napkin-dermatitis

teaching_point: Candidal napkin dermatitis: beefy-red involvement of the folds with satellite papules/pustules — treat with topical antifungal + barrier care.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Napkin dermatitis thrush (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/napkin-dermatitis

teaching_point: More severe napkin rash with erosions — escalate barrier measures, exclude candida/bacterial infection, and review for rarer differentials.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Napkin dermatitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/napkin-dermatitis

teaching_point: Infantile atopic eczema: red, dry, rough cheeks with nasal sparing — classic under-1-year facial pattern (emollients + step-up topical steroid).
dermnet_caption: Infantile atopic dermatitis on the cheeks
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Infantile atopic dermatitis on the cheeks (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/atopic-dermatitis

teaching_point: Active infantile facial eczema with erythema, weeping and early crust — treat inflammation early; watch for secondary infection.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Infantile atopic dermatitis, face (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/atopic-dermatitis

teaching_point: RED FLAG — neonatal HSV: clustered vesicles/erosions in a neonate need urgent same-day assessment, swabs and systemic aciclovir; do not wait.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Herpes simplex (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/blisters-and-pustules-in-neonates

teaching_point: Infantile haemangioma (proliferating): bright strawberry-red superficial plaque on the face — rapid growth in first months; assess site risks.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Infantile haemangioma, face (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/infantile-haemangioma

teaching_point: Involuting infantile haemangioma on the scalp: greying/softening and flattening as the lesion regresses over years.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Regressing infantile haemangioma, scalp (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/infantile-haemangioma

teaching_point: Infantile haemangioma in the napkin/buttock area — high risk of painful ulceration; early specialist input / propranolol often considered.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Infantile haemangioma, buttock (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/infantile-haemangioma

teaching_point: Proliferative preauricular infantile haemangioma — peri-auricular/segmental facial lesions may need PHACES work-up and early treatment.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Preauricular infantile haemangioma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/infantile-haemangioma-complications-and-treatment

teaching_point: Naevus of Ota: slate-blue/grey dermal melanocytosis in the periocular/trigeminal distribution — check sclera; document for future melanoma vigilance.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Naevus of Ota (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/naevus-of-ota-ito-hori

teaching_point: Naevus of Ota involving forehead/temple — congenital or childhood-onset dermal melanocytosis; more common in East Asian skin.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Naevus of Ota (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/naevus-of-ota-ito-hori

teaching_point: Achromic naevus (naevus depigmentosus): stable congenital hypopigmented patch with irregular borders — distinguish from vitiligo (no progression).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Achromic naevus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/achromic-naevus

teaching_point: Segmental hypopigmented naevus on the arm — stable mosaicism pattern; reassure if isolated and child otherwise well.
dermnet_caption: A unilateral depigmented lesion on the arm - the child was otherwise well
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A unilateral depigmented lesion on the arm - the child was otherwise well (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/achromic-naevus

teaching_point: Naevus anaemicus: pale patch due to local vasoconstriction — does not redden on rubbing (diascopy/rub test distinguishes from hypopigmentation).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Naevus anaemicus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/naevus-anaemicus

teaching_point: Becker's naevus: large unilateral brown patch on chest/shoulder that becomes hairy after puberty — epidermal naevus variant.
dermnet_caption: Hyperpigmentation and hypertrichosis over the chest in Becker naevus
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Hyperpigmentation and hypertrichosis over the chest in Becker naevus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/becker-naevus

teaching_point: Becker's naevus on the shoulder girdle with pigmentation and hypertrichosis — usually cosmetic; rarely associated with under-development of underlying tissues.
dermnet_caption: Pigmentation and hypertrichosis in Becker naevus
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pigmentation and hypertrichosis in Becker naevus (© Dr Richard Ashton) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/becker-naevus

teaching_point: Mongolian spot (lumbosacral dermal melanocytosis): blue-grey sacral/buttock patch present at birth — usually fades by early childhood; document to avoid bruise misinterpretation.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Lumbosacral dermal melanocytosis. Mongolian spot (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/lumbosacral-dermal-melanocytosis

teaching_point: More extensive dermal melanocytosis over the lower back — benign; persistent lesions beyond childhood are still usually harmless.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Mongolian spot — lumbosacral dermal melanocytosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/lumbosacral-dermal-melanocytosis

teaching_point: Linear epidermal (verrucous) naevus: warty brown plaque following Blaschko's lines — present from birth/infancy; grows with the child.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Epidermal naevus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/epidermal-naevi

teaching_point: Verrucous epidermal naevus: thickened, papillomatous linear plaque — differential includes ILVEN if inflamed/itchy.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Epidermal naevus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/epidermal-naevi

teaching_point: Port-wine stain (capillary malformation): flat purple-red congenital stain that persists and grows with the child — not a haemangioma; facial V1 risk of Sturge–Weber.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Port-wine stain (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/capillary-vascular-malformation

teaching_point: Port-wine stain on limb/trunk — permanent capillary malformation; differentiate from fading naevus simplex (salmon patch) and from haemangioma.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Port-wine stain (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/capillary-vascular-malformation

teaching_point: Epidermolysis bullosa in a neonate: fragile skin with blisters/erosions from minimal trauma — urgent specialist/EB service referral.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Epidermolysis bullosa (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/blisters-and-pustules-in-neonates

teaching_point: EB clinical example: widespread fragility with denuded areas — severity and subtype (simplex/junctional/dystrophic) guide prognosis and care.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Epidermolysis bullosa (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/epidermolysis-bullosa

teaching_point: EB with acral/trauma-prone blistering — handle gently; non-adherent dressings and multidisciplinary EB nursing are essential.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Epidermolysis bullosa (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/epidermolysis-bullosa

teaching_point: Recessive dystrophic EB: chronic scarring, milia and mitten deformities risk — most severe dystrophic form; tertiary EB centre care.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dystrophic-epidermolysis-bullosa

teaching_point: Aplasia cutis congenita: congenital absence of skin, classically a scalp vertex defect — assess depth, underlying skull, and associated anomalies.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Aplasia cutis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/aplasia-cutis

teaching_point: Aplasia cutis (healed/scarred): atrophic alopecic scar at site of congenital skin defect — document size and refer if large, midline, or syndromic features.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Aplasia cutis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/aplasia-cutis
